text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Young people from wealthy families to lose social benefits as government plans to tighten criteria for income support allowance.
- Many sex telephone workers have joined trade unions, but many employers oppose organised labour in the sector.
- Dairy group Valio pulling 27 tonnes of baby food off shop shelves after fecal bacteria found in porridge.
- Ministry of Finance says joining EMU would not change the present economic policy, but membership would bring stability and eliminate interest-rate and currency disturbances.
- Merita Bank CEO Vesa Vainio has been in the United States this week promoting the bank with big investors. Trade in Merita shares on Helsinki bourse lively this week.

- Enso chief and chairman of Finnish Forest Industries Federation Jukka Harmala said forest industry production will be flat this year, but with prices down by on average more than 10 percent, earnings will be weaker than last year.
- Telecom Finland International, with already 500 corporate clients in Benelux, plans to expand operations to Britain and France next year.
- Interior ministry's top police official says "commando projects" most effective way to recover money lost to white-collar crime -- says raids could net 300 million markka.
- Oat and barley harvest in western Pirkanmaa region better than average, despite fickle summer weather.

- Large volume of alcohol smuggling to Finland and Nordic region continued throughout the summer, but smugglers now trying to sneak in smaller loads due to tougher border controls, customs officials say.
- Tampere tango orchestra "Milonga" invited to international tango festival in Uruguay.
- Low-income groups and the less educated biggest losers if Finland or Sweden joined EMU, says Swedish economics professor and European Parliament member Soren Wibe.
- Finnish UFO watcher says lots of sightings are made in years ending with the number "7" and so he will be looking for contact from outer space next year.
